config.title: Redux Toolkit — createSlice & createAsyncThunk

intro.title: Redux Toolkit — createSlice & createAsyncThunk
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React app that fetches and displays a list of users from a mock API. You'll learn how to manage application state using Redux Toolkit's createSlice and createAsyncThunk. The core programming concept is handling asynchronous operations and state updates in a predictable way with Redux. You'll use TypeScript for type safety, React for the UI, and Redux Toolkit to simplify Redux logic. By the end, you'll understand how to define slices with reducers and async thunks to load data efficiently.
intro.usecase: In real-world applications like e-commerce platforms, createSlice and createAsyncThunk manage complex state for product listings and shopping carts. For example, when users filter products or add items to their cart, these Redux Toolkit utilities handle loading states, errors, and data updates seamlessly. This pattern is essential in dashboards displaying real-time analytics, where asynchronous data fetching and state management must be efficient and predictable. Developers use these tools to build responsive UIs that maintain consistency across user interactions, such as form submissions or live search results.

objectives: Implement a Redux slice using createSlice to manage synchronous state updates
Configure async thunks with createAsyncThunk for handling API operations
Integrate async thunk actions within a slice to manage loading and error states
Initialize a Redux store with the configured slice and thunk middleware
Bind slice actions and async thunks to React components using hooks
Manipulate component state by dispatching both synchronous and asynchronous actions
Render UI elements conditionally based on thunk status (pending, fulfilled, rejected)

steps.title: Define the initial state interface
steps.instruction: Create a TypeScript interface named 'CounterState' with three properties: 'loading' (boolean), 'data' (number), and 'error' (string | null).
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and define each property with its type annotation.
steps.expectedOutcome: A TypeScript interface is defined with the correct property names and types for the slice state.
successCriteria: The CounterState interface exists with 'loading: boolean', 'data: number', and 'error: string | null' properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure all three properties (loading, data, error) are present with the correct types: boolean, number, and string | null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The interface definition is missing or incorrect. Remember to create an interface named CounterState with loading (boolean), data (number), and error (string | null) properties.

steps.title: Create the initial state object
steps.instruction: Create a constant named 'initialState' that matches the CounterState interface, with loading set to false, data set to null, and error set to null.
steps.hint: Use the 'const' keyword to declare a variable named 'initialState' and assign it an object with the three properties from the interface.
steps.expectedOutcome: An 'initialState' constant is created with the correct property values that match the CounterState interface.
successCriteria: The 'initialState' object has properties loading: false, data: null, and error: null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created an initial state object, but check that all three properties (loading, data, error) have the correct values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The initial state object is missing or doesn't match the required structure. Make sure it has loading, data, and error properties with the specified values.

steps.title: Create an async thunk for data fetching
steps.instruction: Create an async thunk named 'fetchCount' using createAsyncThunk from Redux Toolkit. This thunk should simulate fetching data by returning a resolved promise with a value of 5 after a 1-second delay.
steps.hint: Inside the async callback, **return** a `Promise` that **resolves to** `5` after 1000 ms — e.g. `return new Promise<number>((resolve) => { setTimeout(() => resolve(5), 1000); });`. The fulfilled value is what the thunk passes through as the payload.
steps.expectedOutcome: An async thunk named 'fetchCount' is created that simulates data fetching.
successCriteria: The fetchCount thunk is defined using createAsyncThunk, has the correct type prefix, and returns a promise that resolves to 5 after a delay.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your thunk uses createAsyncThunk, has a proper type prefix, and returns a promise that resolves to 5 after 1 second.
steps.feedbackWrong: The async thunk wasn't created correctly. Review the createAsyncThunk syntax and ensure it simulates fetching data.

steps.title: Create a slice with createSlice
steps.instruction: Use createSlice to define a slice named 'counterSlice' with name, initialState, reducers (empty), and extraReducers to handle the async thunk states.
steps.hint: Call createSlice with an object containing name, initialState, reducers (an empty object), and extraReducers (a builder callback).
steps.expectedOutcome: A slice named 'counterSlice' is created with the required structure, ready to handle async thunk states.
successCriteria: The slice is defined with name 'counterSlice', initialState, empty reducers, and extraReducers (builder callback).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you have all four properties: name, initialState, reducers, and extraReducers.
steps.feedbackWrong: The slice is missing required properties or has incorrect structure.

steps.title: Export slice actions and reducer
steps.instruction: Export the slice's actions and reducer from the slice file so they can be imported elsewhere in your application.
steps.hint: Use named exports for the actions and default export for the reducer from your slice object.
steps.expectedOutcome: The slice's actions and reducer are properly exported for use in other parts of the Redux application.
successCriteria: The slice actions are exported as a named export and the reducer is exported as a default export.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've exported something, but check if you're exporting both the actions (as a named export) and the reducer (as a default export) from your slice object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The exports aren't quite right. Remember to export the actions from your slice object and export the reducer as the default export.

steps.title: Configure the Redux store
steps.instruction: Create a Redux store using configureStore from @reduxjs/toolkit, adding your counter slice reducer to the store configuration.
steps.hint: Import configureStore from @reduxjs/toolkit and use it to create a store object with your slice reducer.
steps.expectedOutcome: A configured Redux store is created with your counter slice reducer properly integrated.
successCriteria: configureStore is imported and used to create a store with the counter slice reducer in the reducer configuration.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've imported configureStore and added the counter reducer to the store configuration.
steps.feedbackWrong: The store configuration is missing or incorrect. Check that you're using configureStore with your slice reducer.

steps.title: Create a component to display data
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named CounterDisplay that will display the counter value from Redux. The component should return a div element containing an h2 heading with text 'Counter Value:' and a paragraph showing the current value.
steps.hint: Define a component using either function declaration or arrow function syntax. The component should return JSX with the heading and paragraph elements.
steps.expectedOutcome: A CounterDisplay component is created that returns JSX with a heading and paragraph to display counter data.
successCriteria: The CounterDisplay component is defined with proper TypeScript syntax and returns a div containing an h2 with text 'Counter Value:' and a paragraph element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started creating the component, but make sure it returns the required JSX structure with both heading and paragraph elements.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't properly defined. Create a functional component named CounterDisplay that returns a div with an h2 and paragraph.

steps.title: Use useSelector to access state
steps.instruction: In your CounterDisplay component, use the useSelector hook to extract the 'status' and 'value' properties from the Redux state.
steps.hint: Import useSelector from 'react-redux' and use it to select the counter slice state. The state has a 'counter' property containing the slice.
steps.expectedOutcome: The CounterDisplay component will have access to the current counter state values through useSelector.
successCriteria: The useSelector hook is imported and used to extract both 'status' and 'value' from the Redux state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're extracting both 'status' and 'value' properties from the state.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've imported useSelector and are correctly accessing the counter slice state.

steps.title: Use useDispatch to get dispatch function
steps.instruction: Inside the CounterDisplay component, call the useDispatch hook to get the dispatch function and store it in a variable named dispatch.
steps.hint: Import useDispatch from 'react-redux' if you haven't already, then call it inside the component body.
steps.expectedOutcome: The dispatch function is available inside the CounterDisplay component for dispatching actions.
successCriteria: The useDispatch hook is called inside CounterDisplay and its return value is stored in a variable named dispatch.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're calling useDispatch inside the CounterDisplay component and storing the result in a variable named dispatch.
steps.feedbackWrong: The dispatch function isn't available yet. Remember to call useDispatch inside the CounterDisplay component and store its return value.

steps.title: Add a button to trigger data fetch
steps.instruction: Inside the CounterDisplay component, add a button element with the text 'Fetch Count' that dispatches the fetchCount async thunk when clicked.
steps.hint: Use the dispatch function from useDispatch to call fetchCount with an argument (e.g., 1).

<button onClick={() => dispatch(someAction())}>Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The CounterDisplay component will include a button that, when clicked, dispatches the fetchCount async thunk to fetch data and update the Redux state.
successCriteria: A button element with the text 'Fetch Count' is added inside the CounterDisplay component, and its onClick handler dispatches fetchCount with an argument.

steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but make sure it dispatches fetchCount with an argument when clicked.
